submission.justification: Recommend Radiator-R1 at 2.6 cm because it gives the best simulated 10 GeV/c pion/kaon separation among lifetime-qualified candidates. The best observed separation for R1 is 4.118 sigma at 2.6 cm, exceeding the best R3 result of 3.086 sigma by 1.032 sigma. R2 showed strong prior separation but was excluded from lifetime-stability consideration because it is porous and not hydrophobic-treated; R1 is porous but hydrophobic-treated and is operated under dry nitrogen, so it remains in the lifetime-qualified set.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c.
requirements.evidence: Global best observed result is Radiator-R1 at 2.6 cm with 4.118 sigma separation; next best lifetime-qualified candidate is R3 at 2.975 cm with 3.086 sigma.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: Radiator-R1 is one of the three allowed candidates; R1_candidate_allowed = 1.

requirements.requirement: The radiator must keep its performance over the experiment's lifetime.
requirements.evidence: R1 is not excluded for lifetime stability (R1_exclude_lifetime_stability = 0) and is hydrophobic-treated; the setup operates in dry nitrogen. R2 was excluded, while R1 and R3 remained lifetime-qualified.
Recommended thickness is 2.6 cm, within the allowed 1–6 cm range.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended radiator and thickness.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one option: Radiator-R1 at 2.6 cm.
